# The Cold That Makes the Stars Shine

## Scripture
*"He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds. He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name."* — Psalm 147:3–4 (NIV)

## Reflection
On a clear November night, the stars seem brighter than in summer. This isn't imagination. Cold air holds less moisture, so the atmosphere steadies and the light arrives cleaner, sharper. Winter's chill, it turns out, is what lets us see the heavens most clearly.

Something similar happens in us. We tend to think of hard seasons as spiritual winter—times when God feels distant and the sky of our lives goes gray. But the psalmist places two things side by side: God binding up the brokenhearted, and God naming every star. The same hands that measure the cosmos are gentle with wounds. And often it is the brokenhearted season—the cold, clarifying night—that lets us see God's faithfulness most sharply. Stripped of distractions, we notice light we'd missed before.

The God who calls each star by name has not lost track of you. If He numbers and names what He merely spoke into being, how much more does He hold the heart He formed and redeemed? Your winter is not evidence of His absence. It may be the very weather in which His light becomes most visible.

## Prayer
Lord of the stars, You know each one by name—and You know me. When life feels cold and clear and hard, steady my gaze on You. Thank You that You bind up the brokenhearted and never lose track of Your children. Let this season draw me closer, and let Your light shine brighter in my night. In Jesus' name, amen.
